claim: For the conjugation action of a finite group G of order p^n on itself, the singleton orbits are exactly Z(G), and every non-singleton orbit has cardinality divisible by p; consequently p divides |Z(G)|.
evidence: An element x has a singleton conjugacy orbit iff gxg^{-1}=x for every g in G, equivalently x is in Z(G). By orbit-stabilizer, the orbit size is [G:C_G(x)], which divides |G|=p^n and is therefore a power of p. If the orbit is non-singleton, its size is a positive power of p and hence divisible by p. Partitioning G into conjugacy orbits gives |G|=|Z(G)| plus a sum of multiples of p, so p divides |Z(G)|.
